Tell me how much review time we have from now. I need decisions on which failures count and what clears them, exactly when a locked user can sign in again, and how email resets work during a lockout. For each area, ask the product owner a concrete question and give a test case with an observable outcome. Tell me which decision must be made first and why.

It is 09:30 in Shanghai on March 2, 2026. We have 90 minutes before the 11:00 sign-off.

1. Failure count. Ask whether failures across devices count against one account and whether a successful login clears the count. I would settle account-wide counting first because it determines which attempts can trigger a lockout. If the count is account-wide, fail four times across two devices and confirm the account is unlocked. Fail a fifth time and confirm lockout. In a separate run, sign in after four failures and check that the next failure starts a new count if success clears it.

2. Lockout timing. Ask whether the fifth failure starts the 15-minute timer and whether later attempts extend it. If the timer starts on the fifth failure and does not extend, trigger it at 09:40. Valid credentials must fail at 09:54:59 and succeed at 09:55.

3. Email reset. Ask whether a locked user can complete a reset and whether it clears the lock. Complete a reset during lockout and check whether the new password works immediately or only after expiry, according to the agreed policy.
